Operator: Good day, and welcome to the CommLink Media Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the call. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to CommLink Media Inc.'s Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Lopez, Chief Network Officer; and other members of our leadership team. Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report our results for Q3. We exceeded expectations in several key areas. First, service revenue grew 5.2% year-over-year to $14.8 billion, with wireless up 4.5%, broadband up 7.2%, and enterprise up 3.8%, reflecting the payoffs from our converged 5G and fiber strategy. Second, blended ARPU rose 4.8% to $53.42, driven by targeted pricing actions and bundling with our streaming services that boosted attachment rates significantly. Third, we focused on churn reduction, achieving a blended postpaid rate of 1.42%, down 12% year-over-year, our lowest in over two years thanks to AI-driven retention tools and premium network enhancements. Fourth, operating expense management delivered $285 million in savings, expanding adjusted EBITDA margins by 320 basis points to 42.5%, through network optimization, vendor renegotiations, and SG&A efficiencies. Finally, we are strategically positioning ourselves for long-term growth through $2.4 billion in network investments, accelerating 5G Standalone rollout to 92% coverage in top U.S. markets and expanding edge computing for media synergies.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Alex. Turning to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $15.2 billion, up 5.2% year-over-year. Our adjusted EBITDA was $2.8 billion, resulting in a margin of 42.5%. We are maintaining strict cost discipline. Capital expenditures were $2.4 billion, primarily allocated to 5G rollout and fiber expansion.

Let me unpack our operating expense management initiatives and their impact on profitability in this challenging telecom and media environment, where we're navigating cord-cutting, 5G costs, and streaming competition from players like Comcast and Netflix. These efforts yielded $285 million in year-over-year OpEx savings this quarter, directly fueling our 12% adjusted EBITDA growth and 320 basis points of margin expansion. Network operations optimization drove 45% of savings, or $128 million, via software-defined networking and virtualization, decommissioning 15% of underutilized 4G sites—around 4,200 towers—while shifting to C-band 5G, cutting cell site costs by 22% monthly and energy expenses by $42 million through AI predictive maintenance and Open RAN with Nokia. Procurement and vendor management added $92 million, or 32%, with 18% pricing reductions on handsets, CPE, and CDNs like Akamai, plus consolidating vendors from 1,200 to 850 for $65 million in rebates, crucial as streaming volumes rose 14%. Organizational and SG&A efficiencies contributed $65 million, trimming headcount 4.2% or 3,800 roles via attrition and redeployment, dropping SG&A to 19.2% of revenue, migrating IT to AWS and Azure for 31% data center savings, and closing 120 offices for $28 million annually. In media, content costs fell 16% to $420 million by sunsetting low-viewership channels and shifting to FAST on our LinkStream platform, now at 45 million MAUs generating $150 million in ad revenue, with sports rights renegotiated 11% lower. Regionally, North America saw OpEx intensity drop 9% to 54% of sales, Europe cut 14% via Vodafone JV fiber sharing saving €45 million despite UK price caps, and APAC down 11% with subsidies offsetting content localization rises. These are part of our Efficient Growth 2025 framework targeting $1.2 billion cumulative savings, reinvested in FWA at 2.5 million subs boosting broadband ARPU 8%, and AI personalization cutting churn 22%. Q4 OpEx guidance is $5.6-5.8 billion, flat sequentially, with risks like tower escalators mitigated by zero-based budgeting.

Service revenue, the core of our results, grew 5.2% to $14.8 billion, our strongest in three years, balanced across wireless at +4.5% to $9.2 billion, broadband +7.2% to $3.1 billion, and enterprise +3.8% to $2.5 billion. Wireless benefited from 2.8% postpaid ARPU growth to $52.40, 456,000 net adds to a 112 million base, and low 0.79% churn, with C-band 5G at 85% top MSA coverage via Open RAN, strong U.S. Northeast adds, LATAM JV growth offsetting Europe, and NaaS ramping 15% of mix. Broadband surged on 14.5% fiber growth with 1.2 million FTTH adds to 28 million passed, 3.1% ARPU to $68.20 from multi-gig tiers at 42% mix, XGS-PON at 75% utilization outpacing cable, Southeast U.S. leading, and 62% LinkStream attach adding $4 ARPU, targeting 40 million passed by 2025 amid BEAD. Enterprise wireless up 6.2% with $450 million in 5G private nets for GM and P&G via EdgeCore-AWS, SD-WAN/SASE +22%, North America +5%, EMEA softer, and API/IoT growth at 18% with 52% margins. This validates our converged strategy, with full-year service growth 4.5-5.5%, postpaid adds 1.6-1.8 million, fiber 4.5 million.

On ARPU trends, our blended across mobile, broadband, and media hit $53.42, up 4.8% year-over-year from $50.98, or 5.1% constant currency, sixth straight accelerating quarter beating peers. Mobile postpaid reached $48.75, +5.2%, from 4-6% pricing on Unlimited 5G plans affecting 35% base and 62% bundling take rates on StreamMax at $5 incremental including Netflix/Disney+, lifting $2.15; prepaid $22.40, +2.1%, via data packs with Paramount+. Broadband $68.20, +6.3%, with 7% legacy hikes migrating to fiber bundles at $10-15 premiums, Fiber + Entertainment at 42% penetration adding $4.80, video $32.10 +1.8%. Media $18.75, +9.2%, with GlobalCom TV at 15 million subs, 75% attach. North America $59.80 +6.1% from 5G SA, Europe $42.50 +2.9% bundling Sky/UEFA, emerging $28.90 +7.4% from conversions/FWA. Premium Stack with O-RAN cutting capex/bit 25%, churn to 1.1%, Q4 growth 4-5%.

Churn analysis shows blended postpaid at 1.42%, -12% YoY from 1.61%, sequential from 1.48%, lowest in two years via Stickier Network. Mobile 0.98% down 8 bps, voluntary 0.64% from 5G Ultra at 85% coverage, family plans, AI billing recovering 22%; Midwest pressure offset. Broadband 1.12% -15 bps, FTTH to 12 million passed slashing complaints 40%, bundling +18% retention, NA 1.05%, Europe 1.45%. Streaming 2.45% -28 bps on NexaStream 30 million subs, Content Lock-In with Peacock/UEFA, macro/inflation offset. Trends: 150 bps two-year improvement from $8B capex; ChurnGuard AI predicts 78%, retaining 350k YTD +24%; regions U.S. 1.25%, EMEA 1.65%, APAC/LATAM 1.85%; ARPU add-ons. Outlook sub-1.3% with fiber/5G, NexaLock esports, M&A; supports raised FY24 guidance.

Maria Lopez: Thank you. I would like to provide an update on our network performance. We have made significant progress in expanding our 5G coverage. Our network reliability metrics continue to improve, and we are seeing increased data usage across our customer base. We are also actively working on enhancing our cybersecurity infrastructure. Our team's dedication to high-ROI 5G initiatives has been instrumental in achieving these results.

Network investments are the cornerstone of delivering superior connectivity and media in a data-intensive world. We deployed $2.4 billion in capex, aligning with full-year $9.8-10.2 billion or 18% of trailing revenue, 52% or $1.25 billion to 5G SA rollout, up from 45% prior year, driving ARPU via premium services like low-latency streaming and edge content. Progress exceeds milestones: 92% 5G coverage in top 100 U.S. metros on sub-6GHz C-band (110 MHz from 2021 FCC $3.2B auction), nationwide 68% with 28,000 sites including 4,500 new small cells/Massive MIMO; mmWave densified 1,200 urban sites (NY/LA/Chicago) with Samsung Open RAN boosting efficiency 25%. 65% 5G traffic on SA for URLLC/eMBB slicing, DSS on 3.45-3.55 GHz to 2.5 Gbps peaks; 850 edge nodes with AWS Outposts <10ms latency for 8K/AR/VR, 5G video +320% YoY at 42% mobile data, FWA to 450k households gigabit. NA 85% SA Northeast outpacing T-Mobile; Europe 75% Spain/UK Nokia AirScale, Germany +15% QoQ €450M on spectrum; APAC Jio JV 300M India sub-6/RedCap; LATAM 45% FWA with Claro. Returns: 55% postpaid 5G base, ARPU +4.2% to $58.30 on premium plans/LinkStream; $350M YTD OpEx savings from 70% cloud core/AI energy -18%. Q4 5G capex $1.3B on SA/Open RAN vs Huawei risks; building converged platform for $500B edge by 2028, EBITDA breakeven H2 2025, supply risks hedged $1.1B.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson: Good morning. Can you discuss the competitive landscape and your strategy for managing churn in wireless services?

Alex Rivera: Certainly. In a competitive field with T-Mobile's aggressive plans and Verizon's customizations, our churn strategy leverages the Stickier Network approach, hitting blended 1.42% with mobile at 0.98%, well below industry 1.1%. We've cut voluntary churn via 5G Ultra rollout and AI ChurnGuard predicting 78% at-risk subs, proactive RCS offers retaining 350k YTD. Bundling and regional focus—like Northeast outperformance—offset Midwest pressures, positioning us for sub-1.3% by year-end against Starlink and Big Tech MVNOs.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your expectations for subscriber growth in the next quarter, and how will that impact ARPU trends?

John Ramirez: We anticipate 450-550k postpaid wireless net adds and 1.1 million broadband in Q4, driving blended ARPU growth of 4-5% YoY to around $55. This stems from holiday bundling like StreamMax expansions, fiber passings to 50%, and pricing discipline, with bundles at 62% take rates adding $2+ uplift while compressing churn to 1.1%, ensuring sustainable premiumization.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Patel: Can you provide an update on your fiber deployment plans and the expected ROI on those investments?

Maria Lopez: Absolutely. Fiber is central, with 28 million locations passed up 25% YoY via XGS-PON with Adtran/Calix at 75% utilization, targeting 40 million by YE25 and BEAD synergies. ROI is strong: churn down to 1.12%, ARPU +6.3% to $68.20 from gigabit bundles, 62% streaming attach, margins expanding as symmetrical speeds win vs cable. Capex efficiency from overbuilds in Sunbelt yields payback under 3 years, with FWA complement at 2.5 million subs accelerating broadband growth to 10%+.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Alex, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Alex Rivera: Thank you. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value. Thank you for your time and interest in CommLink Media Inc.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
